svg.title: Who was leased
svg.desc: The state's convicts on 31 December 1894: 614, of whom 512 Black men, 17 Black women, 83 white men and 2 white women. On 1 December 1900: 778, of whom 651 Black men, 23 Black women, 102 white men and 2 white women. In November 1899, 507 of 697 convicts worked in seven phosphate camps, 190 in five turpentine camps.
svg.text: Florida’s state convicts in the reports of the Commissioner of Agriculture; one square = five prisoners. “Colored” is the word of the tables.
512 Black men · 17 Black women · 83 white men · 2 white women
507 in phosphate camps · 190 in turpentine camps
651 Black men · 23 Black women · 102 white men · 2 white women
Sources: Report of the Commissioner of Agriculture 1893–1894, p. 81; 1899–1900, p. 48.
